title: Annotatio I §.II open: First prior Supper controversy — Institution words Hoc est corpus meum needlessly split in two
pass_a_gloss: §. II. Among the prior Protestant Controversies on the Sacred Supper, the first of all is on the Interpretation of the horistic or definitive words of the Institution of the Supper: This is my body: which, that it might appear so much the ampler and fatter, has been needlessly torn by one Protestant party into two, of which the prior asks: Whether literally or κατὰ τὸ ῥητόν? The posterior: Whether properly, or rather improperly, the words of the Sacred Supper — or rather the propositions This is my body and This is my Blood — are to be taken.
pass_b_english: §. II. Of the earlier Protestant Supper controversies, the first is how to read the definitive Institution words: This is my body.
One party has needlessly torn that question in two: whether literally / κατὰ τὸ ῥητόν, and whether the propositions This is my body / This is my Blood are taken properly or improperly.
source_text:
§. II.
Inter priores de S. Coena Controversias Protestanticæs, prima omnium est de Interpretatione verborum Institutionis Coenae horisticorum seu definitivorum: Hoc est corpus meum: Quae ut tanto amplior pinguiorque appareret, ab altera Protestantium parte in duas nequicquam discerpta est, quarum priori quaeritur: Num literaliter vel κατὰ τὸ ῥητόν? Posteriori: Num propriè, an verò impropriè verba S. Coenae, vel potiùs propositiones: Hoc est corpus meum, & Hic est Sanguis meus, capiendae sint.
notes: §.II open; Hoc est corpus meum; needless bifid split.
